dedupe_keys.name: national satellite data centre nsdc of the finnish meteorological institute sodankyla

description: The National Satellite Data Centre of the Finnish Meteorological Institute, run at its Arctic Space Centre in Sodankylä, gives access to the latest satellite data over the Baltic Sea region and the Northern Hemisphere and to products on the changing Arctic environment. The site lists operational data, project data, local observations and archives; the latest optical direct broadcast imagery from MODIS and VIIRS; the SMOS level 3 daily soil freeze and thaw product for the Northern Hemisphere; FinHub, the Finnish Sentinel collaborative ground segment giving complementary access to Sentinel data; COSMO-SkyMed radar data; products such as Baltic Sea ice status, ground frost, hemispheric snow and atmospheric ozone; and project services such as GlobSnow and CryoLand, with a GeoPortal and a virtual cloud service. The centre receives data directly from polar orbiting satellites with its own antennas and also calibrates and validates Earth observation instruments. Access to the listed data is online; no licence or cost is stated on the home page, so terms are set per product. Caveats: parts of the home page still show placeholder text, and product access routes differ between services. Coverage is Finland, the Baltic Sea and the Northern Hemisphere. It supports hazard exposure analysis of snow, sea ice and ground frost for roads, ports and power lines in cold regions; related records are the SYKE open spatial data and the SANSA EO online catalogue.
